page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, translating to 12.0 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench. It demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, reaching 6364.76 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 327.05 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The system excels in data processing, achieving top-tier results in bzip3 decompression, Redis SET operations at 127.0 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 99.89 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for small models, strong performance for medium models, and average performance for large models.

Given its high-density hardware profile, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive deployments by combining high-capacity system memory with dual enterprise-grade GPUs. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is highly suited for workloads such as machine learning training, medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and high-throughput database operations.
